prompts: The owner's gaming rig hitches every few seconds even though the average frame rate looks fine, and the 1% lows are poor. A one-minute frame capture, a sensor log, a dump of the rig's settings and the owner's notes are in {WS}. That rig is not this machine: everything about it is in these files, and nothing is to be applied to this host. Find what causes the hitches and which setting changes fix them within the owner's constraints. Record in {WS}/result.json: avg_fps, low_1pct_fps, cause and changes (a list of {setting, from, to}).
answers:
[goal] Find the hitch cause and setting fix for rig arena-01, record in result.json.

[action] Parsed presentmon.csv (8238 frames) and sensors.csv; correlated frame-time spikes with sensor events; wrote result.json.

[result]
- avg_fps: 137.29 (1000 / mean 7.284 ms, per owner's definition)
- low_1pct_fps: 45.35 (1000 / p99 22.049 ms)
- cause: GPU PCIe link enters ASPM L1 every ~4 s (seconds 2,6,…,58). Each L1 entry produces a burst of 12 slow frames at 22–24 ms. Verified 1:1: all 180 frames >18 ms fall in the 15 L1 seconds; zero slow frames in any other second. The MsMpEng.exe DPC spikes (43–45 s) are a separate, smaller effect.
- change: pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu L1 → disabled (BIOS). This is a power-management setting, not an overclock, so it respects both constraints (link speed stays Gen5 x4; no XMP/PBO/ratio changes).

Evidence: the correlation is exact and bidirectional (no slow frames outside L1 seconds; every L1 second has 12 slow frames). result.json parses cleanly and numbers recompute identically.

[assumptions] 1% low computed as 1000/p99 of MsBetweenPresents with linear-interpolation percentile, matching the owner's stated formula. The L1 transition itself (not the DPC spikes) is the dominant hitch source because the frame spikes align only with L1, not with the 43–45 s DPC window.
